decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent while starting to scale back its monthly bond purchases.

changes.quote: In light of the substantial further progress the economy has made toward the Committee's goals since last December, the Committee decided to begin reducing the monthly pace of its net asset purchases by $10 billion for Treasury securities and $5 billion for agency mortgage-backed securities.
changes.explanation: Because the economy has improved significantly, the Fed is starting to slow down its bond-buying program.

changes.quote: Beginning in December, the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $60 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $30 billion per month.
changes.explanation: The Fed set specific lower targets for adding bonds to its balance sheet starting in December.

changes.quote: The Committee judges that similar reductions in the pace of net asset purchases will likely be appropriate each month, but it is prepared to adjust the pace of purchases if warranted by changes in the economic outlook.
changes.explanation: The central bank plans to keep trimming its asset purchases every month unless the economic outlook changes.

changes.quote: Supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic and the reopening of the economy have contributed to sizable price increases in some sectors.
changes.explanation: The Fed added language acknowledging that supply chain bottlenecks and reopening pressures are driving up prices.

changes.quote: Progress on vaccinations and an easing of supply constraints are expected to support continued gains in economic activity and employment as well as a reduction in inflation.
changes.explanation: Policymakers noted that rising vaccination rates and fewer supply bottlenecks should eventually help lower inflation.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals.

The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.61% APR costs about $60.88 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.6% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.09% would rise by about $6.52 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.7%, and employers added an average of 650k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 5.4% over the past year (September 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.65%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.07% on the day.

whats_next: This statement signals that the Fed is taking its first step away from pandemic-era stimulus by slowing bond purchases while keeping interest rates anchored. Educational forecast models suggest a 77% chance of a hold at the next meeting.
